overview: This extensive file documents U.S. and SCAP regulation of entry into occupied Japan and Okinawa, chiefly from late 1947 through mid-1948. Applications, permits, diplomatic notes, directives, and correspondence reveal how officials managed merchants, missionaries, diplomats, dependents, and other travelers amid quotas, shortages, security concerns, and evolving occupation policy.
interest: The file reconstructs occupation mobility control at case level. It exposes bureaucratic discretion, commercial priorities, gender restrictions, security concerns, and diplomatic inequalities.
